chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abān al-Aḥmar, from Muyassir, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about women: what share do they have of inheritance?
He said: “They have the value of bricks, buildings, wood, and reeds; but as for land and properties, they have no inheritance in them.”
He said: I said, “Then what about clothing?” He said: “The clothing is for them.”

He said: I said, “How did this come to be, while they have an appointed one-eighth or one-fourth?” He said: “Because a woman has no lineage by which she inherits; rather, she is an entrant among them. This was made thus so that a woman does not marry and then her husband, or the children of other people, come and contend with a people regarding their properties.”

key_terms.الثُّمُنُ وَ الرُّبُعُ: the fixed shares of one-eighth and one-fourth in inheritance law
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثِ: inheritance; the estate apportioned to heirs
key_terms.دَخِيلٌ: one who has entered into a family, not originally of its lineage
key_terms.قِيمَةُ الطُّوبِ وَ الْبِنَاءِ وَ الْخَش: the assessed value of bricks, structures, wood, and reeds rather than the items or land itself
key_terms.نَسَبٌ: lineage or kinship connection through which inheritance is linked

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about women inheriting land and property?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the inheritance share of women with respect to structures and movable materials versus land and real estate. It also states the legal rationale given in the narration for this distinction, framing it in terms of lineage and protection of family property.
